SingleToothImplant.title: Can a Single Tooth Implant Be Done?
SingleToothImplant.content1: Single tooth implant application is the beginning of processes that will be completed successfully in a very short time. First, it is checked whether there is sufficient bone tissue for the missing tooth area. The operation is completed in 15-30 minutes. Leaving missing teeth untreated can cause many different problems in the future.
SingleToothImplant.advantagesTitle: What is the Advantage of a Single Tooth Implant?
SingleToothImplant.advantagesContent: In previous years, a single missing tooth was treated with porcelain bridges. For a porcelain bridge, the teeth in front and behind the missing tooth were reduced and used as support pillars. Thus, the bridge and the missing tooth area were treated with a three-unit bridge prosthesis. The advantage of implant treatment in a single missing tooth is that the deficiency is eliminated without touching other healthy teeth. This way, the teeth around the missing tooth continue to function healthily.
SingleToothImplant.boneTitle: Can Implant Treatment Be Applied If There Is Insufficient Bone?
SingleToothImplant.boneContent: One of the factors that most affects the lifespan of an implant is the presence of healthy bone surrounding it. If suitable bone tissue exists, the implant can be placed without any issues. In cases where there is insufficient bone, very successful results are achieved with bone powder or bone graft taken from the patient's own tissue.
SingleToothImplant.priceContent: Price is one of the most frequently asked questions. This pricing varies according to the exchange rates of world-famous dental implant brands from Sweden, Switzerland, Germany, and America. Contact us for the most accurate information.
SingleToothImplant.lifetimeTitle: How Long Is the Lifespan of a Single Tooth Implant?
SingleToothImplant.lifetimeContent: It has been observed that dental implants can remain problem-free in the mouth for 30-40 years, or even a lifetime. The lifespan of an implant depends on many factors. The general health of the individual, and more importantly, oral and dental health directly affect this duration.
SingleToothImplant.recoveryTitle: How Many Days Does It Take to Heal After Implant Treatment?
SingleToothImplant.recoveryContent: What is the healing process like after implant treatment? It varies depending on the size of the operation area, the number of screws placed, the surgical technique, and most importantly, how you manage this process. The healing time for a single implant wound will not be the same as for a bone graft application.

item1.title: Teeth Whitening
item1.subTitle: Orange Dent and Teeth Whitening
item1.value: Orange Dent, with its quality services in dental health and aesthetics, ensures that its patients have the healthiest and most aesthetic smiles. Teeth whitening has become one of the most popular aesthetic dental treatments in recent years. With its expertise in teeth whitening and modern techniques, Orange Dent offers natural, white, and smooth smiles to its patients. Healthy and bright teeth can make a big difference both visually and in terms of self-confidence. Orange Dent provides safe, effective, and fast results, ensuring excellent outcomes in teeth whitening treatment.

item2.title: What is Teeth Whitening?
item2.value: Teeth whitening is a treatment method applied to lighten the color of teeth and achieve a whiter, brighter appearance. Yellowing and stains on teeth usually occur due to smoking, consumption of beverages such as tea, coffee, cola, or aging. Whitening treatment helps remove these stains and yellowing. Orange Dent helps patients regain the natural whiteness of their teeth by offering effective whitening methods.

item3.title: Teeth Whitening Methods at Orange Dent
item3.value: Orange Dent offers personalized treatment plans for patients with different teeth whitening options. The most suitable solution is provided according to the needs of the patients with both office-type whitening and home-type whitening methods.

item4.title: Office-Type Teeth Whitening
item4.value: Office-type whitening is a whitening method applied in a clinical setting by a dentist. Using modern technologies and high-quality whitening products, Orange Dent makes teeth several shades whiter. This procedure usually takes between 45 minutes and 1 hour. The whitening gel is applied to the teeth and activated with a special light or laser. This method provides fast and effective results.
item4.value2: Office-type whitening is ideal for patients who want faster results and prefer to be treated in a professional environment. During the treatment, patients do not feel any pain or discomfort. Orange Dent takes patient comfort into consideration, making the treatment process painless and comfortable.

item5.title: Home-Type Teeth Whitening
item5.value: Home-type whitening is a whitening method that patients can do themselves at home with special whitening kits given by the dentist. This method is generally preferred by those who want to avoid damaging their teeth and manage the treatment process in a controlled manner. Orange Dent offers home-type whitening kits customized according to the patient's teeth. These kits contain whitening gels and mouth trays suitable for the patient's tooth structure.
item5.value2: Home-type whitening is a slightly longer process. However, patients carry out the treatment process in the comfort of their own homes, and the whitening becomes more pronounced over time. Orange Dent offers its patients a safe, effective, and cost-effective option with home-type whitening treatment.

item6.title: Digital Whitening and Advanced Technologies
item6.value: Orange Dent also uses digital technology in teeth whitening treatment to make the treatment process more precise and personalized. With digital whitening simulations, patients can see how their smile will look before treatment. Thanks to this technology, the treatment plan is prepared exactly according to the patient's expectations.

item1.title: In Which Cases Is It Applied?
item1.value: Some discolorations cannot be removed by dental scaling and polishing procedures. In such cases, whitening is required to achieve the desired appearance. Whitening is applied in two main methods: office-type and home-type. Office-type whitening is more commonly applied and recommended due to being performed under the supervision of a physician and achieving results in a short time.

item2.title: What is Office-Type Teeth Whitening?
item2.value: This method, performed under the control of a physician in a clinical setting, is a procedure that takes an average of 45 minutes, depending on the condition of the teeth and the patient's sensitivity. Before the procedure, the mouth should be cleaned by scaling. It is performed using a whitening gel applied to clean tooth surfaces and a powerful light source that activates this gel.

item3.title: Is Teeth Whitening Risky? What is the Success Rate?
item3.value: During the procedure, a gum barrier is used to protect the patient's gums, and specially produced glasses for the whitening process are used to protect the eyes from strong light sources. If the indication for whitening is correctly diagnosed and a good whitening system is used, the rate of achieving the desired result is very high. The permanence of whitening is between 6 months and 2 years, depending on brushing habits and habits such as coffee and smoking after treatment.

item4.title: What Should Be Done After the Procedure?
item4.value: After cleaning, the teeth are more sensitive to staining than normal. Therefore, for the first week, dark-colored foods such as cigarettes, tea, coffee, cherry juice, wine, and tomato paste should not be consumed. Hot and cold foods should be avoided to prevent sensitivity in the first few days. Continue brushing teeth.

item5.title: Does Sensitivity Occur After Teeth Whitening?
item5.value: It is normal to have sensitivity during and for 2 days following the treatment. After the treatment, cream is applied to the teeth to minimize this sensitivity.

item6.title: How Many Sessions Does Teeth Whitening Take?
item6.value: In the standard procedure, it is applied as 3 sessions on the same day. However, sometimes your physician may apply it with follow-up on different days.

item7.title: Does Whitening Harm Teeth?
item7.value: No. Certified, quality agents do not cause any permanent damage to teeth.

item8.title: Whitening agents sold online that I can apply myself. Should I use them?
item8.value: We strongly advise you not to use these products, as all of them have been proven to cause permanent damage to teeth.

item1.title: Wireless Orthodontics (Invisalign)
item1.subTitle: Orange Dent and Invisalign Orthodontic Treatment
item1.value: Orange Dent is a clinic that attaches great importance to aesthetic and functional dental health and aims for the best results with modern dental treatment methods. Invisalign, which offers an ideal solution for patients with aesthetic concerns in orthodontic treatment, is successfully applied by the expert team at Orange Dent. Invisalign is a treatment method using transparent and removable aligners as an alternative to traditional braces. It allows you to have a comfortable treatment process without affecting your appearance while straightening your teeth.

item2.title: What is Invisalign?
item2.value: Invisalign is an orthodontic treatment method using transparent, removable aligners to straighten your teeth. Unlike traditional metal braces, Invisalign aligners are almost invisible and offer a much more comfortable usage in the mouth. Invisalign treatment moves your teeth sequentially, ensuring proper alignment and offers a great aesthetic advantage throughout the treatment process.
item2.value2: Invisalign treatment offers an ideal solution especially for adults and individuals with aesthetic concerns. Thanks to being more comfortable, aesthetic, and practical compared to other treatment methods, Invisalign has become quite popular today.

item3.title: Invisalign Orthodontic Treatment Process at Orange Dent
item3.value: Orange Dent applies Invisalign treatment with personalized solutions specially planned for each patient. In Invisalign treatment, dentists digitally analyze the patient's oral structure and take the necessary steps to start the treatment process. Here is the Invisalign treatment process at Orange Dent:

item4.title: 1. Initial Examination and Evaluation
item4.value: Before starting Invisalign treatment, orthodontists at Orange Dent examine the patient's tooth structure and jaw relationship in detail. The treatment process is planned using X-rays, 3D imaging, and digital analyses. At this stage, the patient's suitability for treatment is determined, and treatment goals are clarified.

item5.title: 2. Personalized Treatment Plan
item5.value: One of the most important steps in Invisalign treatment is creating a personalized treatment plan. Orange Dent uses digital technologies to simulate the movement of each tooth and the treatment process. Thus, detailed information about the treatment process is obtained in advance, and the patient can visually watch how the treatment will progress. This personalized planning ensures the fastest and most effective results.

item6.title: 3. Preparation of Invisalign Aligners
item6.value: After digital scans and measurements are taken, Invisalign transparent aligners are custom-made. Orange Dent prioritizes the quality of aligners used in the treatment process and uses high-quality, reliable materials. Invisalign aligners are changed every two weeks, allowing the teeth to move sequentially.

item7.title: 4. Placement and Use of Aligners
item7.value: After the first Invisalign aligner is placed, the treatment begins. Aligners can be worn by patients throughout the day and removed only while eating or brushing teeth. Orange Dent provides detailed information to patients on how to correctly place and remove aligners and guides them at every stage of the treatment process.

item8.title: 5. Follow-up Appointments and Progress Checks
item8.value: During Invisalign treatment, specialist dentists at Orange Dent regularly monitor patients and follow the progress of the treatment process. Teeth move slowly with each new set of aligners. Throughout the treatment period, new aligners are used every two weeks. Orange Dent performs regular check-ups at every stage of the treatment process to ensure that teeth are moving correctly and the treatment is progressing as planned.

item9.title: 6. Post-Treatment Checks and Results
item9.value: When Invisalign treatment is completed, the dentist at Orange Dent performs a final check evaluating the patient's smile and dental health. When the treatment is successfully completed, patients are recommended to use a retainer. This helps maintain the new position of the teeth and ensures the permanence of the treatment.

item1.title: Root Canal Treatment (Endodontics)
item1.subTitle: Orange Dent and Root Canal Treatment
item1.value: Orange Dent offers comprehensive approach to dental health, providing the highest quality treatment services to its patients. Root canal treatment is a treatment method aimed at saving the tooth in cases where the nerves or canals inside the tooth are infected. Orange Dent uses modern technologies in root canal treatment, offering a painless, fast, and effective treatment process to its patients.

item2.title: What is Root Canal Treatment?
item2.value: Root canal treatment is a procedure performed when the pulp of the tooth, which contains vessels and nerves, is infected or damaged. The pulp is the soft tissue inside the tooth, and when infected, symptoms such as toothache, swelling, and inflammation may occur. Root canal treatment aims to save the tooth and relieve pain by intervening in this infected tissue.

item3.title: Root Canal Treatment Process at Orange Dent
item3.value: Orange Dent uses the latest technology equipment in root canal treatment, offering a fast, painless, and effective treatment process to its patients. The clinic meticulously follows every stage of root canal treatment and always prioritizes patient comfort. The root canal treatment process generally consists of the following stages:

item4.title: 1. Initial Examination and X-ray
item4.value: Root canal treatment begins with a detailed examination and X-ray to obtain a clear assessment of the tooth's condition. Orange Dent uses digital X-ray technology to visualize the tooth's internal structure in detail. Thus, infected areas and treatment needs are determined.

item5.title: 2. Cleaning the Tooth and Preparing the Canal
item5.value: In the first step of root canal treatment, the infected tissue is cleaned with special instruments. Orange Dent uses advanced anesthesia methods to ensure patients do not feel pain. After the inside of the tooth is cleaned, the canal area is shaped and disinfected.

item6.title: 3. Filling the Canal
item6.value: After the inside of the tooth is cleaned and shaped, the canal area is filled with a biocompatible material. This material preserves the natural structure of the tooth and prevents recurrence of infection. Orange Dent uses high-quality and safe materials to ensure the tooth remains healthy for a long time.

item7.title: 4. Restoration of the Tooth
item7.value: After root canal treatment is completed, a permanent filling or crown is placed on the tooth. This procedure restores the function of the tooth and provides a natural appearance aesthetically. Orange Dent offers restoration options compatible with the aesthetic structure of the tooth, ensuring a perfect smile after treatment.

item1.title: Is Root Canal Treatment a Painful Procedure?
item1.value: No. With local or block anesthesia, patient comfort is very high.

item2.title: How Many Sessions Does Root Canal Treatment Take?
item2.value: This entirely depends on the condition of the tooth. Today's technology has made single-session endodontic treatments possible; however, the condition of the root may sometimes necessitate medication and healing between sessions.

item3.title: Is Root Canal Treatment Expensive?
item3.value: No. Because not treating the existing condition will lead to much more burdensome treatment costs.

item4.title: Are Root Canal Treatment and Filling Different Things?
item4.value: Yes. Filling is applied in cases where the pulp tissue is not affected, at the enamel and dentin level. The vessel and nerve tissue of the tooth are not interfered with. In root canal treatment, the pulp chamber is cleaned and filled, and a filling is placed on the top of the tooth. So every root canal treatment includes a filling; but not every filling requires root canal treatment.

item1.title: Gum Treatments (Periodontology)
item1.subTitle: Orange Dent and Gum Treatment
item1.value: Orange Dent is a clinic specialized in its field, aware that gum health is as important as dental health. Gums are one of the fundamental building blocks of our oral health. Since gum diseases can cause serious health problems that may lead to tooth loss, timely treatment is very important. Orange Dent offers a healthy and safe treatment process to its patients with state-of-the-art equipment and expert staff in gum treatment.

item2.title: What is Gum Treatment?
item2.value: Gum treatment is a treatment process applied in cases of inflammation, swelling, bleeding, and more serious problems of the gums. Gums are the tissues that support and surround the teeth. Healthy gums hold your teeth properly and firmly. However, gum diseases, especially gingivitis and periodontitis, can lead to tooth loss if left untreated.

item3.title: The main symptoms of gum diseases are:
item3.value: - Gum bleeding, especially during brushing or flossing
item3.value6: Gum diseases can be treated at an early stage, but more comprehensive treatments are required at advanced stages. Orange Dent offers effective treatment methods for each stage, ensuring patients regain healthy gums.

item4.title: Gum Treatment Process at Orange Dent
item4.value: Orange Dent performs gum treatment by planning it individually according to each patient's needs. The gum treatment process consists of the following steps:

item5.title: 1. Initial Examination and Evaluation
item5.value: The first step of the gum treatment process is a comprehensive examination by dentists. Specialist dentists at Orange Dent evaluate the health of the gums, determine the level of gum disease, and create a treatment plan. If necessary, X-rays are taken, and the depth of gum inflammation is measured.

item6.title: 2. Gum Cleaning (Scaling)
item6.value: In the first stage of gum diseases, it is important to clean the plaque and tartar accumulated on the gums. At Orange Dent, dentists clean plaque and tartar on your teeth with professional scaling method. This cleaning helps reduce gum inflammation and makes gums healthy.

item7.title: 3. Deep Gum Cleaning (Root Planing)
item7.value: If gum disease is at a more advanced level, a deep cleaning procedure called root planing is applied. In this procedure, infected plaques and tartar settled under the gums are cleaned. Orange Dent uses this treatment to smooth root surfaces and restore gums to health. Root planing is a critical step to bring gums back to a healthy level.

item8.title: 4. Gum Surgery (If Necessary)
item8.value: When gum diseases progress, more advanced treatment methods may be needed. At Orange Dent, permanent damage to the gums can be repaired with gum surgery. Various surgical techniques can be applied to improve gums aesthetically and functionally. For example, in patients with gum recession, gum reconstruction or strengthening with soft tissue grafts can be achieved.

item9.title: 5. Follow-up Appointments and Care

item2.title: What is Frenectomy?
item2.value: Frenum is a thin tissue attached to the gums, lip, or underside of the tongue. The most common types of frenum in the mouth are known as labial frenum (the frenum connecting the upper lip to the gums) and lingual frenum (the frenum under the tongue). These frenums usually do not prevent proper tooth development, but sometimes when these frenums are overstrained or abnormally large, they can cause various problems.
item2.value2: Frenectomy is the surgical removal of these abnormal frenums. Orange Dent usually performs frenectomy to eliminate problems such as decay, separation of teeth, feeding and speech difficulties caused by excessive tension of the lip or tongue frenum.

item3.title: When is Frenectomy Necessary?
item3.value: Frenectomy may be necessary in the following cases:
item3.value2: 1. Tongue-tie (Ankyloglossia): When the frenum under the tongue is too short, tongue mobility becomes limited. This can negatively affect speech, swallowing, and even dental hygiene. Orange Dent corrects this condition by applying frenectomy in patients with ankyloglossia.
item3.value3: 2. Lip Frenum Problems: If the upper lip has a frenum too close to the gums, it can cause spacing between the teeth. This leads to aesthetic and functional problems. Orange Dent can surgically remove the lip frenum to solve such problems.
item3.value4: 3. Swallowing and Speech Problems: Short or tight frenums can make correct swallowing motion and proper speech difficult. Orange Dent performs frenectomy to eliminate such problems, improving patients' quality of life.
item3.value5: 4. Oral Hygiene Problems: A short frenum can make cleaning between teeth difficult, which can lead to cavities. Orange Dent eliminates cleaning problems between teeth with frenectomy.

item3.title: What is the difference between bridge and implant treatment?
item3.value: In bridge treatment, healthy teeth next to the missing tooth are used as supports, while in implant treatment, a titanium implant is placed directly into the jawbone in place of the missing tooth. item1.title: What are the symptoms of teeth grinding (Bruxism)?
item1.value: The most common symptoms include
item1.value2: Jaw pain, headache, or tension in the temples felt upon waking in the morning.
item1.value3: Cracks, fractures, or visible wear on the enamel layer of the teeth.
item1.value4: Increased tooth sensitivity to hot and cold foods.
item1.value5: Clicking sounds from the jaw joints and difficulty opening and closing the jaw.

item2.title: What causes Bruxism?
item2.value: Although patients often see it as a dental problem, the actual cause can usually develop independently of the teeth. While there is no single cause, the main triggers are:
item2.value2: Stress and Anxiety: Daily life stress, anger, or intense anxiety are among the biggest triggers.
item2.value3: Sleep Disorders: Conditions such as sleep apnea or snoring can reduce sleep quality and increase bruxism.
item2.value4: Dental Structure (Malocclusion): Misalignment of the upper and lower teeth, missing or crooked teeth.
item2.value5: Lifestyle: Excessive alcohol, smoking, or caffeine consumption.

item3.title: How is teeth grinding treated?
item3.value: Night Guard (Occlusal Splint): Transparent plaques custom-made by a dentist prevent teeth from rubbing against each other during sleep. Night guards are intended more to prevent possible dental and joint problems rather than curing bruxism itself.
item3.value2: Botox Treatment: Botox applied to the chewing muscles (masseter muscle) reduces the excessive pressure involuntarily exerted by the muscles and is currently considered the most effective treatment method.
item3.value3: Stress Management: Methods such as psychological counseling help reduce the underlying source of stress.
item3.value4: Muscle Relaxants: For a certain period (between 3 to 5 months), muscle relaxants taken before bedtime as recommended by your doctor can help prevent involuntary teeth grinding at night.
item3.value5: Dental Restorations: Inappropriate, dysfunctional, or outdated dental restorations can be corrected and/or filling or crown treatments can be applied.

item1.title: Same-Day Dental Implant
item1.subTitle: Risks, Benefits, and Procedure
item1.value: Being toothless during the process of getting new teeth can be uncomfortable and embarrassing, especially if we are in working life. Waiting for your new dental prosthesis is just annoying.
item1.value2: At this point, same-day dental implants come to our rescue.
item1.value3: Many people around you, even you, may have had dental implants. However, sometimes the waiting period for a new dental prosthesis is long and annoying. Therefore, same-day 'immediate' dental implants are an excellent option for many patients.
item1.value4: Let's take a closer look at this idea...
item1.value5: • Comparison of immediate and traditional implants

item2.title: Immediate Dental Implants vs Traditional Implants
item2.value: When your dentist talks about 'immediate' implant, they mean placing the implant at the same time as extracting the tooth and even placing a temporary prosthesis on it.
item2.value2: In traditional dental implants, this process works as follows; when you lose a tooth, you must wait at least 1 month before applying a dental implant to that area. At the end of this period, after the implant is placed, there is another 3-month waiting period. With the construction of your dental prosthesis, this total period is 4 to 5 months.
item2.value3: Although it emerged primarily for aesthetic purposes, it provides many advantages to the patient and dentist in terms of function and time. Also, immediately loaded implants can be functional. This means that with the implants you have on that day, you can eat soft foods and brush them. You can have a full dental prosthesis in one day. This means that this method can be valid not only for a single tooth but also for multiple teeth or all your teeth.
item2.value4: One type of immediately loaded dental implant is the All-On-4 concept. This procedure means placing four implants in the jawbone to support your entire prosthesis and placing a temporary prosthesis on the same day. In the All-On-4 procedure, the dentist places a temporary prosthesis on the implants for a natural appearance while the implants integrate with the bone.
item2.value5: The difference between immediate dental implants and traditional implants is the time between implant placement and prosthesis placement. In traditional implants, your dentist may want to wait at least 3 months before placing the prosthesis on the implant. Because your bone needs to accept and integrate with the implant.
item2.value6: In an immediately loaded dental implant, the dentist places a temporary porcelain immediately after placing the implant. In a traditional dental implant, it can take 3-6 months between implant placement and porcelain placement.
item2.value7: While a standard dental implant can take months to complete, an immediate dental implant can provide a new dental prosthesis on the same day.

item3.title: Same-Day 'Immediate' Dental Implants - Who is a Candidate?
item3.value: If you want an immediate dental implant, you need to talk to your dentist to see if you are suitable. First of all, your dentist will likely put you through a very comprehensive screening process to see if you are suitable.
item3.value2: You must have good oral health and general physical health. This means that if you smoke, have an autoimmune disease, have chronic systemic disorders, or have hygiene problems, you cannot get immediate implants immediately.
item3.value3: Also, if you suffer from teeth grinding (bruxism) or clenching, immediate implants may not be the best solution for you, as these can affect the long-term prognosis and success rate of implant treatment.
item3.value4: Basically, if you want to get a dental implant - immediate or traditional - having a healthy body alone may not be enough. You must also pay attention to your oral hygiene. Yes, it has been reported that 10% of initially successful dental implants are lost within the first 10 years due to poor oral hygiene.
item3.value5: If you have good oral and physical health and do not smoke, you may be a candidate for immediate implants even if you have an autoimmune disease or use prescription bisphosphonate drugs (prescribed for advanced bone loss). To be sure, be sure to report these and talk to your doctor.

item4.title: What Kind of Dentist?
item4.value: So, what kind of dentist performs immediate dental implants?
item4.value2: Any dentist who performs dental implants can also perform same-day implants, but not every dentist can do them.
item4.value3: So first you should talk to your preferred dentist. The reason not every dentist performs immediate dental implants is that they do not want to take various risks. A complication can jeopardize the implant and the dentist's reputation.
item4.value4: Immediate dental implants have many associated risks, so you need to talk to your dentist to see if they are a good option for you.

item5.title: Same-Day Dental Implant Risks
item5.value: Here are some risks and potential complications associated with immediate dental implants. For these reasons, some dentists do not offer this service.
item5.value3: For an immediate dental implant to be successful, the implant must not move at all. Therefore, the procedure itself is very sensitive. The dentist must place the implant in a way that it never moves. For this, in addition to the quality of the patient's jawbone, the experience of the physician comes to the forefront.
item5.value5: An immediate dental implant needs to integrate with strong bone and must likely withstand a certain torque (tightening force of the implant). The best candidates for immediate implants are people with relatively healthy and strong bones.
item5.value7: The risks of immediate implants are no different from other dental procedures. When a dentist performs any surgical procedure (tooth extraction, gum surgery, etc.), there will be risks and possible complications. Risks such as implant failure, infection, and pain are all possible complications of implant surgery.
item5.value8: As with standard dental implants, the biggest risks of immediate dental implants include implant movement, implant failure, pain, and infection.

item6.title: Benefits of Same-Day Dental Implants
item6.value: At the same time, the benefits of the immediate dental implant procedure are many. Here are some benefits of immediate dental implants.
item6.value3: The obvious benefit of the immediate dental implant procedure is that it is completed in just one visit, sometimes several visits. This significantly reduces both the time spent in the dentist's chair and the time spent without teeth. Remember, traditional implants and prostheses can take 3 to 6 months.
item6.value4: Gums Adapt Better to the Prosthesis
item6.value5: Because the prosthesis is placed immediately on the implant, the gums usually grow around it and shape accordingly, making it look more natural. However, in traditional dental implants, after 3 months, the gum may need to be reopened and reshaped for prosthesis placement.
item6.value6: The benefits of immediate dental implants are clear: they are faster, involve one surgery, and the gums grow and shape better around the prosthesis.
item6.value7: We must not forget that while the success of traditional implants depends more on the physician, the success of immediate implants depends on the compliance of the physician and the patient. The success rate of immediate implants is almost the same as traditional implants.
item6.value8: Immediate implants allow you to get your new teeth faster. This means you don't have to spend a long time with missing teeth.

item7.title: Same-Day Dental Implant Procedure Step by Step
item7.value: So how do they perform dental implants in one day?
item7.value2: First of all, your dentist will put you through a comprehensive examination. This is where your jaw and dental X-rays will be taken, they can answer your questions and summarize what will happen to you. Also, if deemed necessary, your dentist may perform some diagnostic tests such as CT scans and photographs of your mouth. They will analyze the images and essentially make a draft of your mouth and procedure plan.
item7.value3: Every part of the surgery must be planned with specific steps and objectives in mind. It is necessary to make unnecessary and very high promises to the patient.
item7.value5: First, although dentists prefer local anesthesia, you may sometimes receive anesthesia that allows you to sleep during large-scale surgeries. After numbing, they will begin the procedure.
item7.value6: Using a guide, they will place the implant into the jawbone. This step is relatively quick.
item7.value7: Immediately after surgery, they will place a temporary dental prosthesis. Placing and fitting the prosthesis takes relatively much more time than placing the implant.
item7.value9: After the anesthesia wears off, you will feel some pain and discomfort. Pain, swelling, or some bruising is a very natural and normal result of this process.
item7.value10: The good news is that the dentist will prescribe painkillers and give you ice packs. The best thing you can do during this period is to make sure you take your painkillers and other medications regularly, and rest. Despite all this, if you have unexpected bleeding, swelling, or persistent pain, be sure to call your doctor.
item7.value11: The procedure for immediate dental implants is: administration of anesthesia, cleaning the surgical area, placing the implant into the jawbone, then immediately placing the dental prosthesis.
item7.value12: All these procedures may vary depending on your health condition, the strength of your jawbone, and the experience of your dentist.
item7.value13: However, remember that every dental surgery - even for dental implants - has pros and cons, benefits and risks, and after weighing all aspects of immediate implants, you and your dentist can choose the best one for you.

Implants.whatistypofImplants: What are the Types of Implants?

typofImplants.item1Content: One of the most preferred materials in terms of natural tooth appearance and aesthetically beautiful appearance is ceramic dental implants. Due to metal allergy occurring during treatment in some of our patients, ceramic implants can also be preferred instead of titanium implants. Since ceramic material is also considered biocompatible, it prevents additional complications in the jawbone and mouth, providing attachment to the body like titanium.

item1.title: What Does Dental Implant Mean?
item1.value: Dental implants are metal (usually titanium) screws surgically placed into your jawbone under the gums. These screws act as the foundation feet on which your dentist will place dental prostheses.

item2.title: How Do Dental Implants Work?
item2.value: The working principles and forms of dental implants have changed a lot over the years. However, regardless of how they function, the basic goal is to look and function like natural teeth. That is, they should be aesthetically satisfying as well as allowing you to eat comfortably. In addition, they should be easily cleanable in practice.

item3.title: A dental implant has three main parts

value.title: Dental implants consist of a screw (placed into the jawbone), an abutment (attached to the implant with a screw), and a crown (attached to the abutment and looks like a natural tooth).

item1.title: Screw (made of titanium or zirconium)
item1.value: This is the implant itself and is placed inside your jawbone. Since your implant will remain inside your jawbone, you can only see it with dental X-rays. It wouldn't be wrong to simply compare a dental implant to a screw dowel. All intermediate parts that will hold the dental prosthesis are attached to the implant with a screw.

item2.title: Abutment
item2.value: It is the intermediate part that connects your implant and the prosthetic tooth to be made. Like a screw entering a dowel, it is screwed into your implant.

item3.title: Crown
item3.value: This is your prosthetic tooth. It is not attached directly to your implant. It is attached to the intermediate abutment part.

value.title: If you are considering getting a dental implant, let's examine together what path you should follow.

item1.value: First, your dentist will numb the area where the implant will be placed with local anesthesia. This means that only that area will be numbed. In very rare cases, your dentist may decide to perform the procedure under general anesthesia (complete sedation).

item2.value: Second, your dentist will prepare your jawbone and surrounding tissues for implant placement.

item3.value: Your dentist will place your implant in the most suitable area. The most ideal place and the most suitable place may not be the same. This means that your dentist may make various changes, either in advance or during the surgery, by informing you if they can foresee it.

item4.value: After the anesthesia wears off, it is normal to have some pain in the jawbone and some bleeding in the mouth.

item5.value: After the implant is placed, the integration process with your jawbone will begin, called 'osseointegration'. The bone will completely surround the implant and become very solid.

item6.value: Your dentist will recommend a healthy diet of soft and not too hot foods.

item7.value: If your dentist deems it appropriate, they may give you a temporary prosthesis to use during this process. But remember that this may not always be possible.

item8.value: After the osseointegration period is completed (probably between 3 and 6 months), your dentist will take measurements to start the dental prosthesis. Then, the dental prosthesis from the laboratory is attached to the abutment placed on the implant.

item9.value: Remember that the procedure is slightly different for same-day dental implants.

itemplus1.title: Who Can Get Dental Implants?
itemplus1.value: Having good general health and clean oral hygiene is very important for an implant. After that, if you have enough bone to support an implant, you may be a good candidate for a dental implant. Sometimes artificial bone powder called 'bone graft' may be necessary.
itemplus1.value2: If you have a chronic disease or an autoimmune disease, your dentist may request some tests before implant placement.
itemplus1.value3: Also, smoking will greatly affect the success rate of the implant. The negative effects of smoking on wound healing have been clearly demonstrated. You need to have meticulous oral hygiene before, during, and after implant placement.
itemplus1.value4: Most people without chronic or autoimmune diseases who do not smoke excessively or drink alcohol are not at risk for dental implants.

value.title: There are two main types of dental implants

item1.title: 1. Standard Dental Implants:
item1.value: Their sizes start from 8 to 10 mm. A certain bone thickness and height are required.

item2.title: 2. Shorter Dental Implants:
item2.value: Their sizes start from 4 mm. They are implants developed for areas where there is insufficient bone height. Their manufacturing procedures are slightly different. They can be the most ideal solution for cases where bone graft is not suitable.

item6.title: Single Tooth Implants
item6.value: A single tooth implant replaces the root of a missing tooth. It allows a prosthetic tooth to be made only in that area. This is not only for aesthetics but also prevents damage to adjacent teeth, prevents natural teeth around from shifting over time, and even helps prevent bone loss. A single tooth implant is an independent unit and does not involve treatment of adjacent teeth, preventing them from being cut and damaged.

value.title: Dental implants help support a dental prosthesis when you are missing one or more teeth (even if all your teeth are missing). An implant-supported bridge uses implants instead of receiving support from other surrounding teeth. The type of dental implant your dentist chooses will vary according to your condition. This means that one patient's dental implant cannot be the same as another.
value.subTitle: In traditional implant bridges, dental prostheses are cemented to the abutment on the implant. This has two disadvantages.

item1.value: First; when the prosthesis needs to be replaced or a problem is encountered in the future, the only thing that can be done is for your dentist to remove the prosthesis by hitting it with a mini hammer. There is of course a risk that these hammer blows may damage your implant and even your jawbone.

item2.value: Second; fixing your dental prosthesis to your implant with cement can lead to odor problems in the future because 'this cement will dissolve over time'. This is the main reason why patients complain that their dental prostheses smell over the years.

item3.title: Screw-Retained Implant Bridges:
item3.value: have small holes on the dental prostheses. Your dentist fixes the prostheses onto the implants using mini screws. This allows the prosthesis to be removed without causing problems in the future and prevents odor. However, this system brings additional cost. You should definitely discuss this with your dentist and decide together.

item8.title: Pros and Cons of Dental Implants
item8.value: Although every surgical operation has pros and cons and dental implants are completely safe, they also have pros and cons.

item9.title: Pros
item9.value: Unlike traditional prostheses, dental implants fuse and integrate with your jawbone. This allows you to put pressure on your artificial teeth like natural teeth and eat. Dental implant prostheses are generally more comfortable than standard prostheses or bridges. Implant-supported prostheses do not require interfering with surrounding teeth, as in traditional prostheses or bridges. Thus, they allow dental prosthesis to be made without damaging adjacent teeth. Beyond all this, having a dental implant helps preserve your jawbone. When teeth are missing for a long time, the jawbone begins to resorb. This necessitates the need for bone grafts. In more advanced cases, your entire jaw and even your facial structure may become deformed.

item10.title: Cons
item10.value: The biggest downside of getting an implant is cost. As in almost every country in the world, general health insurance does not cover implants as a 'cosmetic' elective procedure (like zirconium crowns, teeth whitening, etc.) in our country. The most reasonable way to reduce dental treatment costs is to go to your dentist for regular check-ups as much as possible. It should be well known that every postponed dental problem leads to bigger problems and thus much higher costs. A dental problem that can be easily and cheaply solved at the beginning will, if postponed, lead to greater financial burdens as well as a more difficult and longer process. Of course, dental implants are not perfect and flawless. They can fail due to various reasons such as smoking, an autoimmune disease, or uncontrolled diabetes. They can also cause the implant to become loose or painful, in which case they may need to be removed.

ImplantsFinaly.value: Dental implants may seem like a painful procedure because they are screwed into your jawbone. But you will not feel pain because local anesthesia (or general anesthesia depending on the situation) will be applied.
ImplantsFinaly.value2: Dental implant prostheses are much safer and more comfortable than traditional prostheses in the long term. They usually do not move and feel like natural teeth.
ImplantsFinaly.value3: Dental implants are the most comfortable, safest, and newest way to restore function (eating and drinking), phonation (speech), and aesthetics.
ImplantsFinaly.value4: In addition to all these, dental implants are not miracles. You must definitely heed your doctor's warnings and give adequate importance to your oral hygiene.

ImplantHealingProcess.title: Dental Implant Surgery Healing Period
ImplantHealingProcess.subTitle: Diet, Pain Management, and Other Tips
ImplantHealingProcess.value: Dental implant surgery is a procedure that should be taken seriously. No one wants it, but like any other type of surgery, it requires a recovery period.
ImplantHealingProcess.value2: After one or more dental implants are placed, the patient's adherence to warnings and the dentist's experience will determine the healing process. However, the healing time may vary depending on the difficulty of the surgery area, how well you take care of yourself, and how your body reacts to the implant. It should be remembered that each individual's response to surgery is different.
ImplantHealingProcess.value3: We will cover all these and more below.

item1.title: Dental Implant Duration
item1.value: What is the recovery time after dental implant surgery?
item1.value2: Generally, it takes 5-7 days for all symptoms to subside. However, some patients may experience longer healing times due to different factors (bone powder addition, sinus lift, etc.).
item1.value3: Some of the reasons why your healing time may vary are:

item2.title: How Many Implants Did You Have?
item2.value: Your healing time may vary depending on whether you have a single implant, multiple implants, or All-On-4 implants. Basically, more implants mean more and larger surgical areas, which means a slightly longer healing time.

item3.title: Sinus Lift
item3.value: Sinus lift surgery can also prolong your healing time. This is a surgery where artificial bone powder is added when there is insufficient bone tissue in the upper molar area. The dentist will need to move (or lift) the sinus membrane upward for the additional bone to settle.

item4.title: Bone Grafting
item4.value: Bone grafting is necessary when your jawbone is not thick enough to secure an implant. After getting the implant, chewing forces put a lot of pressure on the bone, so it needs to be as strong as possible.
item4.value2: If you need a bone graft, your dentist will take bone from another part of your body (like your hip) and transplant it to your jawbone. They may also use artificial bone.
item4.value3: In either case, an extra few months are needed for healing. However, if minimal bone grafting is required, it may not take that long.

item5.title: Osseointegration
item5.value: Osseointegration is the process of integration of your jawbone with the dental implant. This takes time to happen successfully 'and may differ for each patient'. Therefore, the dentist may predict different times for each patient depending on bone tissue quality, patient's age, patient's systemic disorders, and medications the patient regularly uses.
item5.value2: Assuming the procedure goes well and there are no complications afterward, the healing period should last about a week to ten days. The complete integration of the implant into the bone can be estimated as 3 months.

item6.title: The First Few Days After Dental Implant Surgery
item6.value: Now that we have covered the recovery timeline, let's discuss what the recovery process will look like, what you can do to make it successful, and how to speed it up.
item6.value2: What to Expect on the First Day?
item6.value3: During the first 30 minutes after surgery, you will want to hold firm but gentle pressure on the gauze packs with your bites. This will keep them in place.
item6.value4: For almost everyone, bleeding stops within the first 30 minutes. If you are still bleeding after 30 minutes of firm pressure, place new gauze for another 30 minutes. After that, you should change the gauze every 30 to 45 minutes until bleeding stops.
item6.value5: Some symptoms you may experience on the first day include:
item6.value10: All these are expected signs that your body is healing itself.
item6.value11: Here are some dental implant recovery tips to follow to speed up your healing and minimize pain:
item6.value12: • Be careful not to disturb the surgical areas
item6.value13: • Gently brush your teeth with a toothbrush on the night of the surgery
item6.value14: • After 24 hours, rinse with salt water 2-3 times a day
item6.value17: On the second and third days after surgery, your body will continue to heal itself, but you need to take care of your mouth to help the process.
item6.value18: You may see a greenish-yellowish discoloration or bruising around the surgical areas, but this is normal and should only last 2-3 days after surgery. After that, you can apply moist heat to the area to reduce discoloration.
item6.value19: If you feel a sharp ridge or an edge of your tooth, this is also common. If it concerns you, don't hesitate to contact your dentist.
item6.value20: You may also experience dry lips, sore throat, and stiff jaw muscles, all expected symptoms of having gauze in your mouth. All of these should disappear after about 2-3 days.
item6.value21: Here are some general instructions for caring for implants in the days following the procedure to help your recovery period:
item6.value22: • Rinse your mouth with salt water, taking five minutes to use a full 8-ounce glass. You can do this as often as you like, at least twice a day.
item6.value23: • Gently brush your teeth as soon as possible after the procedure. You may not be able to brush with normal force (or want to) due to pain and swelling. But maintaining good oral hygiene during this recovery period is important.
item6.value24: Another thing to consider during recovery is modifying your diet, which we will discuss in the next section.
item6.value25: During the recovery period, you will likely experience oozing, bleeding, swelling, and pain. You will also want to maintain good oral hygiene.

item7.title: Dental Implant Healing Diet
item7.value: It is a smart idea to temporarily change your diet to help your mouth heal quickly and properly. It doesn't sound fun, but it can be very helpful.
item7.value2: The best thing you can do with your diet is to avoid direct contact with the implant as much as possible for as long as possible. This means no hard foods until the area is completely healed.
item7.value3: Foods You Should (and Should Not) Eat After Surgery
item7.value4: Generally speaking, you should eat mostly soft foods while trying to chew on the opposite side of your mouth from where the implant was placed.
item7.value5: Here are some food ideas that are good to eat after surgery:
item7.value15: On the flip side, there are many foods to avoid immediately after surgery:
item7.value16: • Hard foods like chips, nuts, or apples
item7.value17: • Acidic foods like tomatoes, lemon, lime, orange juice
item7.value20: Stick to soft and mushy foods during recovery, and avoid hard, sticky, and spicy foods.

item8.title: Conclusion
item8.value: Now that you have read this article, you know what to expect after your dental implant surgery, the expected recovery time, potential symptoms, and what you can do to make the whole process easier.
item8.value2: Along with your doctor's recommendations, you should be ready for the dental procedure you need.

item1.title: Bone Graft for Dental Implants
item1.value: Bone graft, or artificial bone powder as it is commonly known. Doesn't sound very pleasant at first, does it?
item1.value2: You may have been frightened after learning what a bone graft is. But there is really nothing to fear - dentists do them all the time.

item2.title: Now let's learn together what a bone graft is...
item2.value: Types

item3.title: Is Bone Graft Necessary for Implants?
item3.value: Bone grafting is when a dentist takes bone from another place and places it into the implant site. It is not always necessary.
item3.value2: Bone graft placement is a procedure where a dentist places artificial bone or bone taken from another area to support and/or create a thicker area for implant placement.
item3.value3: Just as a thick and solid wall is preferred over thin and weak drywall when inserting a screw, implants also need to be supported by bone of sufficient thickness and density to provide long-term reliable support for the teeth to be made.
item3.value4: Although common, bone grafts for dental implants are not always necessary.
item3.value5: If your dentist sees that your jawbone is too thin, soft, or insufficient, they will likely talk about a bone graft. In cases where there is insufficient bone, the implant will fail in the long term, even if not initially.
item3.value6: Your dentist may take bone from another area and place it into the implant site, or if this is insufficient or impossible, they may apply a completely artificial bone graft.

item4.title: Does Bone Graft Affect Treatment Time?
item4.value: If a bone graft is applied, this will affect the overall course and time of your treatment. Since there are many stages when getting a dental implant, adding a bone graft will both extend the time and bring additional costs.
item4.value2: Bone grafting can extend your treatment time by a few months (3 to 6 months), but this depends on how much graft is applied, where it is placed, and the type of dental prosthesis planned.
item4.value3: However, many times a bone graft is a necessary and mandatory step.

item5.title: Types of Dental Implant Bone Grafts
item5.value: A graft bone can be taken from your own body such as the jaw, back of the jaw, hip, or leg. These are known as 'autografts' because they come from your own body.
item5.value2: Sometimes the bone can be an 'allograft' from a cadaver source. This type of bone is specially processed to eliminate any bacteria or other biological material. Since this bone is completely sterile, the risk of rejection is very low or none, and the bone grafting procedure can be performed without a secondary surgical site on your body. However, they are the most expensive grafts.
item5.value3: Bone graft can also come from animal sources such as cattle and is known as 'xenograft'. Bone from animal sources is just like bone from a human source and undergoes a series of processes to make it safe for use.
item5.value4: Your dentist's decision on which bone graft and in what proportion to use may vary depending on the method and amount that will be best for you. There are also different sizes of bone grafts depending on how much is needed.

item6.title: Minor Bone Graft
item6.value: Your dentist may use a minor bone graft after extracting damaged teeth. This means placing bone graft in granular form (looks like coarse sand) into the empty tooth socket.
item6.value2: Then, using sutures, they close the cavity with a protective membrane 'collagen membrane'. In the following weeks, natural bone will form inside the tooth socket, preserving the original bone height. This process takes about a month (depending on your systemic disorder, smoking-alcohol use, oral hygiene).

item7.title: Moderate Bone Graft
item7.value: A moderate bone graft is needed when more significant bone loss has occurred and both height and width are insufficient.
item7.value2: The dentist will make a small incision in the required bone area and then place sufficient bone granules. This procedure will help create the necessary space to place the implant and will provide width and height as it heals.

item8.title: Major Bone Graft
item8.value: When a person loses multiple teeth for a long time, they will often experience a significant amount of bone loss. In such cases, dentists may recommend a major bone graft.
item8.value2: To increase the likelihood of the material used adapting to the bone tissue in the implant area, your dentist may prefer to use a bone block from elsewhere on your body instead of using artificial bone powder.
item8.value3: They fill small areas needed to create a smooth surface with bone granules. Then they completely close the entire area using sutures. Using bone granules of this size will extend the time we wait for dental prosthesis by 3 to 6 months.

item9.title: Sinus Lift (in the upper jaw)
item9.value: Another type of bone graft is called a 'sinus lift'. It is a very common condition in the upper jaw molar areas. In cases of multiple tooth loss in these areas, excessive bone loss and/or downward sagging of the sinuses may be seen.
item9.value2: Dental implants cannot be placed into a hollow area (sinus), so the dentist will need to lift the sinus floor to fill this space.
item9.value3: They will make an incision from the edge of the gum and open a small window into the sinus cavity. The dentist carefully separates and lifts the sinus membrane from the sinus walls. Then, artificial bone powder is placed between the membrane and the sinus floor.
item9.value4: When sufficient bone tissue is placed in the area, the dentist covers it with a membrane 'collagen membrane' to protect the artificial bone tissue. Then the small window opened is completely closed with sutures.
item9.value5: When the implant will be placed is an important issue. If you have minimal bone thickness to keep your implant initially stable, your implant is also placed at the same time, and your dental prostheses can be made after a waiting period of at least 6 months. However, in some cases where not even that much bone is present, the implant is placed after waiting 4-6 months for the sinus lift to fully heal. Then there is a 3-month waiting period after the implant is placed. After this period, dental prosthesis construction can begin.
item9.value6: These durations and which method your implant will be applied with should be started after your dentist decides what is best for you.

item10.title: What Happens After the Bone Grafting Procedure?
item10.value: At the end of your dental implant process; experiencing swelling in your gums, mild bruising on your face and skin, oozing of blood, pain, and discomfort is a natural result of this procedure. If you encounter such situations, we advise you not to panic or worry. This means your body is healing itself, and it needs time to do so.
item10.value2: Your dentist will prescribe some medications for your pain as well as antibiotics to prevent infection. Follow your dentist's recommendations and take medications as directed.
item10.value3: Avoid trying alternative treatments or medications without consulting your dentist first, as they may have side effects you may not be aware of.
item10.value4: If any of these situations seem excessive to you or if you have non-stop bleeding or unrelieved pain, be sure to contact your dentist for advice. They may increase your painkiller dose or suggest some other solutions.

item11.title: Healing of Bone Graft
item11.value: As mentioned above, the healing time can vary, lasting from a few months to a year. It may vary depending on what your procedure involved, how the integration of the implant into your jawbone (osseointegration) is going, and the methods used. Sometimes your dentist may extend or shorten the time initially predicted.
item11.value2: The success rate of dental implants worldwide is very high, around 95%. In our country, this rate is around 96%. However, we must say that it is definitely not 100%. It is very important that you do everything you can to help this process at every stage. Make sure to strictly follow all your dentist's recommendations and prohibitions.
item11.value3: For example, your doctor may ask you to eat only soft foods to avoid pressure on the surgical areas. Also, you need to have very good oral hygiene to help the healing process and to avoid problems with the implant integrating with the bone.
item11.value4: Smoking immediately after oral surgery is definitely not recommended. Tobacco smoke negatively affects the healing process and can cause the graft to heal more slowly and even fail. Studies have shown that smoking, alcohol, and poor oral hygiene are the biggest reasons for dental implant failure.
item11.value5: Systemic health problems such as uncontrolled diabetes also negatively affect the healing process.
item11.value6: Your dentist will inform you about possible risks and give recommendations before the bone graft procedure and implant surgery.

item12.title: Some things you can do to take care of your natural teeth as well as your dental implant:
item12.value: • Brush, floss, and rinse with non-alcoholic mouthwash 2-3 times a day. We also recommend using special dental implant brushes that can reach places a toothbrush or floss cannot.
item12.value2: • Do not skip regular check-ups with your dentist, preferably every six months. This ensures your implant heals properly and continues to perform well.
item12.value3: • Avoid tobacco and excessive caffeine as they can damage both natural and artificial teeth.

item13.title: Possible Complications
item13.value: Dental grafts are safe when performed by a licensed and experienced dentist. Remember, the majority of implants (95%) are successful, and many involve bone grafts.
item13.value2: However, as with any surgery, complications may occur in bone graft and dental implant applications, although rare. Some potential risks to be aware of include:
item13.value4: • Damage to natural teeth, blood vessels, or nerves
item13.value5: • Numbness, tingling in lips, tongue, and cheeks

item14.title: Bone Grafting Cost
item14.value: The cost of a bone graft can vary depending on the type of graft used, the amount of bone needed, and the surgical site. Sinus lift operations for upper jaw implants are more difficult and complicated cases than many other areas. Therefore, they will increase the cost. In addition, costs may vary according to the knowledge and skill of the dentist you consult.
item14.value2: • Bone graft is when a dentist takes bone from another place and places it into the implant site. It is not always necessary, but may be necessary depending on the type of dental prosthesis your dentist plans for you.
item14.value3: • There are four main types of bone grafts: minor, moderate, major, and sinus lift. Which one is applied to you depends on how much bone is needed.
item14.value4: • Like any surgery, bone graft applications can lead to swelling, pain, and discomfort during the healing period.
item14.value5: • As with any surgery, complications such as infection, pain, swelling, and numbness can occur in bone graft applications.
item14.value6: • Bone graft surgery requires from a few months to a year to heal.
item14.value7: • If you need a bone graft for a dental implant, this will bring additional costs.

item1.title: Gum Recession and Sensitivity
item1.value: You should visit your dentist at least once every six months. These regular check-ups allow you to prevent many oral problems at an early stage. In these check-ups, tooth decay and gum recession are the most common findings that patients are not yet aware of.
item1.value2: Although gum recession sometimes manifests itself immediately with sensitivity, it can sometimes be overlooked with no or very few symptoms. Gum recession can lead to serious consequences, including tooth loss, in the long term.
item1.value3: In this article, we will discuss together what you should do and what path to follow without worrying too much if you have gum recession.

item2.title: First, what is gum recession?
item2.value: Gum recession means the gum tissue surrounding the teeth pulls away from the roots of the teeth. First, it should be well understood that as the gum recedes, the jawbone surrounding the tooth also recedes with it, meaning it begins to erode.
item2.value2: Gum recession leads to two major problems.
item2.value3: The first; as everyone knows, it leads to sensitivity. This can reach levels that affect life standards, even making it impossible to take tap water into the mouth.
item2.value4: Secondly; as gum recession accompanies bone loss, teeth will start to loosen over time. In advanced stages of gum recession, it can lead to tooth loss. This is like a tree that loses its soil due to erosion, its roots become exposed, and eventually it has to fall. This is a situation you often hear around you. 'I had no decay, but I lost my tooth because it became loose, I had to have it extracted'

item3.title: What causes gum recession?
item3.value: Gum Disease (gingivitis)
item3.value2: Gum disease (gingivitis) is a bacterial infection of the gums that damages gum tissue and the bone around your teeth. Also called gingivitis, gum disease is the leading cause of gum recession. About one-third of adults have this problem.
item3.value3: Gum disease is generally caused by plaque accumulation around gum tissue, some autoimmune diseases, medications that cause dry mouth, and smoking.
item3.value5: Regardless of how well some of us care for our teeth, we are more prone to gum recession. Here, genetic systemic disorders (such as diabetes, heart disease, etc.) play a very important role.
item3.value7: Brushing your teeth with too much pressure or using a hard-bristled toothbrush can irritate your gums and lead to recession. This is often seen in smokers who apply a lot of pressure to remove tobacco stains. Also, some individuals may have naturally yellower or darker teeth. In such cases, people may brush harder, consciously or unconsciously, to make their teeth whiter. In both cases, they only damage their gums and also cause abrasion (concave wear) on the surfaces of tooth roots.
item3.value9: Not brushing, flossing, and using antibacterial mouthwash allows plaque on teeth to turn into tartar. Tartar buildup pushes gums away from the tooth and causes inflammation. Tartar deposits create a space or pocket between the gums and the tooth, providing an ideal environment for bacterial growth and gum disease.
item3.value11: If you are a woman, hormonal fluctuations during puberty, menstruation, pregnancy, and menopause can make your gums more sensitive and lead to recession.
item3.value13: Whether it's cigarettes, chewing tobacco, or hookah, tobacco forms a sticky plaque on teeth that is difficult to remove and causes gum recession. Remember, the plaque on your teeth turns into tartar and creates those pockets that cause bad bacteria to multiply between the tooth and gums.
item3.value15: Stress in our lives often causes teeth grinding. Grinding and clenching put excessive pressure on our teeth and the surrounding bone, irritating and inflaming the ligaments holding teeth in their sockets. This irritation can cause gums to become more sensitive and recede. It also causes tooth loosening along with bone loss around the tooth.
item3.value17: When we bite, if they don't all come together at the same time, there is a problem. This means that too much pressure is applied to the gums and bone in the areas of the mouth where the teeth first contact when biting. Excessive biting force irritates and inflames gums, causing gum recession.
item3.value19: Gaps can form between our teeth due to tooth loss or gum recession. Food trapped in these gaps not only causes bad breath but also irritation and inflammation in the gums and underlying bone. This inflammation causes further gum recession.
item3.value21: A blow or injury can also cause irritation, inflammation, infection, and gum recession. Similarly, a fishbone piercing or a hard edge of bread injuring the gum can cause infection and inflammation.

item4.title: What Can I Do About Gum Recession?
item4.value: A dentist considers three treatment levels when treating gums.
item4.value3: Level I treatment is treated only with prescription in the early stages of gum recession. Recession at this level easily resolves with twice-yearly teeth cleaning and good oral hygiene.
item4.value4: Depending on the source of gum irritation, simply eliminating the cause may be sufficient. Brush twice a day correctly with a medium-hard toothbrush and use dental floss. If teeth clenching or grinding is causing gum recession, talk to your dentist about a mouth guard to reduce the load on your teeth when clenching and grinding. If you use tobacco, do your best to quit. It should be known that even if you receive the best treatment and go to the best dental clinic, if you continue to use tobacco, everything done will either be unsuccessful or gum problems will start again.
item4.value6: Early mild gum recession is relatively easier to treat. In this case, you may need to visit your dentist two or three times. First, standard scaling and polishing will be done. If cleaning is not enough; then deep cleaning is performed on the affected area after 7 days. This procedure is to clean plaque and tartar accumulated below the gum level. The dentist will also prescribe an antibiotic to clean the remaining bacteria in the area.
item4.value8: Level III treatment for receded gums involves surgery and is therefore the most invasive. Necessary if the spaces and pockets between the gum and tooth are very deep or if there is significant bone loss. There are three different surgical options: open flap technique, regeneration, and soft tissue graft. Your dentist will decide the best option for you.
item4.value10: If your doctor decides that the open flap technique is the best option to treat your gums, they make small incisions in the affected areas to minimize the depth of pockets between the gum and tooth. They align the gum tissue with the root of your tooth.
item4.value12: If the bone supporting your teeth has decreased, your dentist may consider this method to regenerate or replace lost bone and tissue. After separating the gum tissue from your tooth, the dentist places a regenerative material in the affected area to help the missing bone and gum tissue return to their natural level.
item4.value14: In this procedure, soft tissue is removed from an adjacent tooth that has sufficient gum tissue or the palate or roof of your mouth. This tissue is then sutured to the gum tissue at the site of gum recession.
item4.value15: Although it may not be the most important event of your day, there are measures you can take to at least correct existing gum recession and stop further damage. Now that you know you have gum recession, consult your dentist to plan a recommended treatment plan. These chompers have to last you the rest of your life, and a beautiful smile is the best asset.
